units.source_excerpt: As Wordle has become popular on social media, more and more users have played the scrabble game. How do time and word attributes affect the number of reports, distribution of attempts, and other report-related information?
units.reusable_pattern: As [subject] has become popular, more and more [actors] have [action]. How do [factors] affect [outcomes]?
reusable_elements: As [subject] has become popular, more and more [actors] have [action]. How do [factors] affect [outcomes]?
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'more and more' as unquantified growth claim

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, a modeling analysis was conducted using the game data from 2022.
units.reusable_pattern: Therefore, a [analysis] was conducted using [data]
reusable_elements: Therefore, a [analysis] was conducted using [data]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid empty 'therefore' with no prior causal claim

units.source_excerpt: Before building the model, we cleaned and normalized the given data and identified word attributes such as the number of repeated letters, number of vowel letters, number of consonant letters, commonness, and frequency.
units.reusable_pattern: Before building the model, we [cleaned] and [normalized] the given data and identified [attributes] such as [list]
reusable_elements: Before building the model, we cleaned and normalized the given data and identified [attributes] such as [list]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list attributes without saying how they were measured

units.source_excerpt: First, to predict the number of future reports, a prophet-based time-series prediction model was built, considering the effects of trends, seasonality, and holidays. The predictions yielded a range of report numbers for March 1, 2023: [10355,18742].
units.reusable_pattern: First, to predict [target], a [model] was built, considering [effects]. The predictions yielded a range [interval]
reusable_elements: First, to predict [target], a [model] was built, considering [effects]. The predictions yielded [interval]
prohibited_generalizations: State confidence level with the interval

units.source_excerpt: Regarding the variation of report numbers, during the week, the number of reports tends to be highest on Wednesdays and lowest on weekends.
units.reusable_pattern: Regarding [variation], during [period], [quantity] tends to be highest on [day] and lowest on [day]
reusable_elements: Regarding [variation], [quantity] tends to be highest on [day] and lowest on [day]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say 'tends to' without the seasonality plot

units.source_excerpt: In exploring the effect of word attributes on the proportion of difficulty reports, we calculated higher-order partial correlation coefficients for both, controlling for the interaction between word attributes, and found that the number of vowel letters was negatively correlated.
units.reusable_pattern: In exploring [effect], we calculated [coefficients], controlling for [interaction], and found that [attribute] was [direction] correlated
reusable_elements: In exploring [effect], we calculated [coefficients], controlling for [interaction], and found [signed correlation]
prohibited_generalizations: Report the coefficient, not only the sign

units.source_excerpt: Secondly, an optimized multi-objective regression prediction framework was developed to explore the effects of word attributes on the distribution of reported outcomes. The framework chose the optimal lasso regression to predict the test set with an RMSE of 0.80.
units.reusable_pattern: Secondly, an optimized [framework] was developed to explore [effects]. The framework chose the optimal [algorithm] with an RMSE of [value]
reusable_elements: Secondly, an optimized [framework] was developed. The framework chose [algorithm] with RMSE [value]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not personify the framework as choosing the model

units.source_excerpt: The ranking importance of each attribute was calculated, and it was found that the number of consonant letters, number of vowel letters, and frequency had a more significant influence on the distribution of reported results with the influence factors of 4.226, 3.993, and 1.253, respectively.
units.reusable_pattern: The ranking importance of each [attribute] was calculated, and it was found that [list] had a more significant influence with factors [values], respectively
reusable_elements: The ranking importance of each [attribute] was calculated, and it was found that [list] had influence factors [values], respectively
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'more significant' without a significance test

units.source_excerpt: Next, the above model was used to predict the distribution of reported outcomes for each word in the 5-letter word set. Then, K-means was used to classify the words into high, medium, and low difficulty categories based on the average number of attempts.
units.reusable_pattern: Next, the above model was used to predict [target] for each [item]. Then, [algorithm] was used to classify [items] into [levels] based on [metric]
reusable_elements: Next, the above model was used to predict [target]. Then, [algorithm] classified [items] into [levels] based on [metric]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent difficulty cutoffs without stating the rule

units.source_excerpt: The model's accuracy is 91.36% by matching the attribute intervals for different difficulty words, and it can be inferred that the established model and the divided attribute intervals are reasonable.
units.reusable_pattern: The model's accuracy is [value] by matching [intervals], and it can be inferred that [model] is reasonable
reusable_elements: The model's accuracy is [value] by matching [intervals]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer 'reasonable' from one accuracy number

units.source_excerpt: Finally, the sensitivity analysis results demonstrate that our model is robust and reliable. In addition, the study of the data set also revealed the declining popularity of Wordle and the increasing percentage of difficult mode challenges.
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, [analysis] results demonstrate that our model is robust and reliable. In addition, the study revealed [finding-A] and [finding-B]
reusable_elements: Finally, [analysis] demonstrate that our model is robust and reliable. In addition, the study revealed [findings]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid pairing 'robust and reliable' without the perturbation table

units.source_excerpt: Keywords: Wordle analysis, Prophet, High-order partial correlation, Multi-objective regression forecasting, K-means
units.reusable_pattern: Keywords: [comma-separated method list]
reusable_elements: Keywords: [domain], [model], [statistic], [framework], [cluster]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the problem name as a keyword

units.source_excerpt: Crossword puzzles have always seemed inseparably linked to the media. Since January 2022, Wordle, the New York Times' digital crossword, has become more and more popular in many countries.
units.reusable_pattern: [Genre] have always seemed inseparably linked to [domain]. Since [date], [subject] has become more and more popular in [scope]
reusable_elements: [Genre] have always seemed inseparably linked to [domain]. Since [date], [subject] has become more popular
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'always seemed' and 'inseparably linked' as unsupported history

units.source_excerpt: How do players play Wordle? They are permitted to select five letters from a pool of 26 to construct a five-letter word that can be solved in no more than six attempts.
units.reusable_pattern: How do [actors] [action]? They are permitted to [constraint] that can be solved in no more than [N] attempts
reusable_elements: How do [actors] [action]? They are permitted to [constraint] in no more than [N] attempts
prohibited_generalizations: Prefer direct rule statement over a question the paper then answers

units.source_excerpt: By using the available data wisely, we can solve some interesting problems.
units.reusable_pattern: By using the available data wisely, we can solve some interesting problems
reusable_elements: By using [data], we can solve [named problems]
prohibited_generalizations: Replace 'wisely' and 'interesting' with the actual tasks

units.source_excerpt: Considering the background information, constraints outlined in the problem statement and additional guidance, we need to solve the following problems.
units.reusable_pattern: Considering [background], constraints outlined in [source] and [guidance], we need to solve the following problems
reusable_elements: Considering [background] and constraints in [source], we need to solve the following problems
prohibited_generalizations: Drop 'additional guidance' if none is cited

units.source_excerpt: Based on the analysis of the problem, we propose the model framework shown in figure 1, which is mainly composed of the following parts.
units.reusable_pattern: Based on the analysis of the problem, we propose the model framework shown in Figure [N], which is mainly composed of the following parts
reusable_elements: Based on the analysis of the problem, we propose the framework in Figure [N], composed of the following parts
prohibited_generalizations: Name the parts in the sentence, not only after the figure

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 1. Assume that the user data given in the question is independently and identically distributed. Reason 1: this assumption ensures that the individual samples are independent of each other.
units.reusable_pattern: Assumption [N]. Assume that [claim]. Reason [N]: this assumption ensures that [benefit]
reusable_elements: Assumption [N]. Assume that [claim]. Reason [N]: this assumption ensures [benefit]
prohibited_generalizations: A reason that restates the assumption is not a justification

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 3. Assume that the external environment associated with the game does not change abruptly. Reason 3: external factors remain steady to ensure stable prediction models.
units.reusable_pattern: Assume that [environment] does not change abruptly. Reason: [factors] remain steady to ensure stable [models]
reusable_elements: Assume that [environment] does not change abruptly so that [models] stay stable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume away the trend the model is built to explain

units.source_excerpt: Table 1: Notations. Symbol, Definition. sj timestamp, k growth rate, delta-j amount of change in the growth rate, m offset, epsilon error term.
units.reusable_pattern: Table [N] lists symbols with one-line definitions for the forecasting model
reusable_elements: Table [N]: Notations. [symbol] [definition]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define symbols only in a table

units.source_excerpt: Topic C reports on the use of Wordle in the past year. However, we found a lot of dirty data in this report.
units.reusable_pattern: [Source] reports on [topic]. However, we found a lot of dirty data in this report
reusable_elements: [Source] reports on [topic]. However, we found dirty data
prohibited_generalizations: Replace 'a lot of dirty data' with the error count

units.source_excerpt: The two words numbered 525 and 314 do not match the game because they are only 4 in length, so we inferred that the dataset blundered by under-entering the letters.
units.reusable_pattern: The [items] do not match [rule] because [evidence], so we inferred that the dataset [error-type]
reusable_elements: [Items] do not match [rule] because [evidence], so we inferred [error-type]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the dataset 'blundered'

units.source_excerpt: We use the 68-95-99.7 rule (3 sigma criterion) to screen and reject outliers. We found an anomaly in the Number of reported results data for the word study on 2022/11/30, and we zeroed it.
units.reusable_pattern: We use the [rule] to screen and reject outliers. We found an anomaly in [series] and we [action] it
reusable_elements: We use the [rule] to screen outliers. We found an anomaly on [date] and [correction]
prohibited_generalizations: Zeroing a count is not the same as rejecting an outlier

units.source_excerpt: Combining Wordle's gameplay and reviewing the analysis information of the relevant games, we classify the attributes of words into the following points.
units.reusable_pattern: Combining [gameplay] and reviewing [sources], we classify the attributes of [objects] into the following points
reusable_elements: Combining [domain knowledge] and [sources], we classify [objects] into the following attributes
prohibited_generalizations: Cite the reviewed sources or drop the claim

units.source_excerpt: When players play Wordle, the first words are often chosen as AUDIO and LEFTY because this includes all the vowel letters AEIOU. In the composition of words, vowel letters are easily known and, therefore, easily guessed.
units.reusable_pattern: When [actors] [action], the first [choices] are often [examples] because [coverage]. [Feature] are easily known and, therefore, easily [outcome]
reusable_elements: When [actors] start, they often choose [examples] because [coverage]. [Feature] is therefore easier to guess
prohibited_generalizations: A player heuristic is not evidence that the attribute predicts scores

units.source_excerpt: Although neural network models have become increasingly popular in recent years, this model usually requires a large amount of data for training. A dataset with only 400 or so data is not a good place to consider a neural network model.
units.reusable_pattern: Although [popular method] have become increasingly popular, this model usually requires [resource]. A dataset with only [N] is not a good place to consider [method]
reusable_elements: Although [method] is popular, it usually needs [resource]. With only [N] observations, [method] is a poor fit
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reject neural nets from sample size alone

units.source_excerpt: On balance, we decided to use the Prophet model, an algorithm based on an additive model for predicting time series data with characteristics such as seasonality, trends, and holidays.
units.reusable_pattern: On balance, we decided to use [model], an algorithm based on [structure] for predicting [data] with [characteristics]
reusable_elements: On balance, we decided to use [model], based on [structure], for [data] with [characteristics]
prohibited_generalizations: Name the alternatives that were balanced

units.source_excerpt: The Prophet algorithm models each of the model's three components and then combines them to generate the forecast data.
units.reusable_pattern: [Algorithm] models each of the [N] components and then combines them to generate [output]
reusable_elements: [Algorithm] models each component and then combines them to generate [output]
prohibited_generalizations: State the combination rule

units.source_excerpt: We choose a trend term based on a segmented linear function. We set n changepoints to 25 and changepoint prior scale to 0.05. For seasonal trends, we set seasonality prior scale to 10.
units.reusable_pattern: We choose [component] based on [form]. We set [parameter] to [value] and [parameter] to [value]
reusable_elements: We choose [component] based on [form]. We set [parameter]=[value]
prohibited_generalizations: Justify hyperparameters or mark them as defaults

units.source_excerpt: When selecting a data range, it is usually necessary to consider the order of magnitude of the data. Therefore, we screened the original data and selected data from after May 5, 2022.
units.reusable_pattern: When selecting [range], it is usually necessary to consider [criterion]. Therefore, we screened [data] and selected data from after [date]
reusable_elements: When selecting [range], consider [criterion]. We therefore kept data after [date]
prohibited_generalizations: A start-date cut needs a sensitivity check

units.source_excerpt: The model predicts a range of 10355 to 18742 for the number of reports on March 1, 2023.
units.reusable_pattern: The model predicts a range of [low] to [high] for [quantity] on [date]
reusable_elements: The model predicts a range of [low] to [high] for [quantity] on [date]
prohibited_generalizations: Attach the interval width that produced the range

units.source_excerpt: Figure b shows the weekly cyclical pattern, with significantly more people playing Wordle on Wednesdays. The number of weekend reports tends to be lower.
units.reusable_pattern: Figure [label] shows the [pattern], with significantly more [actors] [action] on [day]. [Opposite] tends to be lower
reusable_elements: Figure [label] shows [pattern], with more [action] on [day] and less on [day]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say 'significantly' without a test

units.source_excerpt: From the above table, we can see that the p-values of the significance tests are almost all weakly correlated, and only the total ranking of word frequency is strongly correlated. This result is not satisfactory.
units.reusable_pattern: From the above table, we can see that [tests] are almost all [weak]. This result is not satisfactory
reusable_elements: From Table [N], [tests] are mostly [weak]. This result is not satisfactory
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a null result unsatisfactory and then hunt for a method that rejects it

units.source_excerpt: To sum up, we chose the algorithm of higher-order biased correlation analysis to do correlation analysis on the percentage of each attribute with the difficulty pattern.
units.reusable_pattern: To sum up, we chose [algorithm] to do [analysis] on [target]
reusable_elements: To sum up, we chose [algorithm] for [analysis]
prohibited_generalizations: 'To sum up' needs a real summary, not a method swap

units.source_excerpt: In general, the higher-order partial correlation coefficient, after taking the absolute value, is no correlation when it is 0-0.09, weak when 0.1-0.3, moderate when 0.3-0.5, and strong when 0.5-1.0.
units.reusable_pattern: In general, [metric], after taking the absolute value, is [label] when it is [band]
reusable_elements: In general, |[metric]| is [label] on [band]
prohibited_generalizations: Cite the convention or treat bands as author-defined

units.source_excerpt: Since the amount of data given in the question is very small, we give up using neural network to predict it, and instead use an optimized multi-objective regression prediction framework to process it.
units.reusable_pattern: Since [data] is very small, we give up using [method-A] and instead use [method-B]
reusable_elements: Since [data] is small, we do not use [method-A] and instead use [method-B]
prohibited_generalizations: 'Give up' is informal for a method rejection

units.source_excerpt: All these regression models can perform well for small data while being able to handle multiple classification tasks and suitable for incremental training. In addition, their well-adaptive ability, self-learning ability, and generalization ability also meet our requirements.
units.reusable_pattern: All these [models] can perform well for [setting] while being able to [capabilities]. In addition, their [ability list] also meet our requirements
reusable_elements: These [models] fit [setting] and support [capabilities]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stack 'adaptive, self-learning, generalization' without tests

units.source_excerpt: From the output of the above figure, we can find that the root mean square error of the LASSO regression algorithm is the smallest, and the total average root mean square error of its multiple repeated fits is only 0.8, which can show that our regression model can predict the data very well.
units.reusable_pattern: From the output, we can find that [algorithm] has the smallest [metric], only [value], which can show that our model can predict the data very well
reusable_elements: From [figure], [algorithm] has the smallest [metric], [value]
prohibited_generalizations: RMSE 0.8 does not by itself mean 'very well'

units.source_excerpt: The excellent property of LASSO regression is that it can produce sparsity, which can reduce some insignificant regression coefficients to zero for the purpose of eliminating variables.
units.reusable_pattern: The excellent property of [method] is that it can produce [property], which can reduce [coefficients] to zero for the purpose of [goal]
reusable_elements: [Method] produces [property], setting some coefficients to zero and dropping variables
prohibited_generalizations: Drop 'excellent'

units.source_excerpt: We take the average of multiple fits as the final prediction to make the results more accurate.
units.reusable_pattern: We take the average of multiple fits as the final prediction to make the results more accurate
reusable_elements: We average multiple fits as the final prediction
prohibited_generalizations: Averaging does not automatically increase accuracy

units.source_excerpt: In order to get the word attributes that have a more significant influence on our prediction model, we propose an analysis based on Permutation Importance.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to get [target], we propose an analysis based on [method]
reusable_elements: To identify [target], we use [method]
prohibited_generalizations: Permutation importance is applied, not proposed

units.source_excerpt: Generally speaking, the prediction accuracy is considered high when the RMSE does not exceed 2.
units.reusable_pattern: Generally speaking, [quality] is considered [label] when [metric] does not exceed [threshold]
reusable_elements: Generally speaking, [quality] is considered [label] when [metric] does not exceed [threshold]
prohibited_generalizations: An RMSE cutoff of 2 is meaningless without units and scale

units.source_excerpt: We think that the average number of tries can represent the difficulty level of a word, but since the data set given in the question is too small, it would affect the performance of the clustering analysis.
units.reusable_pattern: We think that [metric] can represent [concept], but since [data] is too small, it would affect [analysis]
reusable_elements: We treat [metric] as a proxy for [concept]. The given sample is too small for clustering, so we [expansion]
prohibited_generalizations: 'We think' is not a definition

units.source_excerpt: As illustrated in the table above, both Silhouette Coefficient and DBI are decreasing slightly as the number of clusters increases. To improve the accuracy of identifying word difficulty, we choose to cluster into 3 classes.
units.reusable_pattern: As illustrated in [table], both [metric-A] and [metric-B] [trend] as [parameter] increases. To improve [goal], we choose [setting]
reusable_elements: As Table [N] shows, [metrics] move as [parameter] increases. We choose [setting]
prohibited_generalizations: A slight decline does not by itself justify K=3

units.source_excerpt: Analysis of the results shows that Number of duplicates, Maximum of repeats, Prevalence, and Frequency vary widely in different classifications.
units.reusable_pattern: Analysis of the results shows that [attributes] vary widely in different classifications
reusable_elements: The results show that [attributes] differ across classes

units.source_excerpt: It is easy to find that its attributes are all in the difficult range we have classified. Therefore, we believe that the word EERIE belongs to the difficult interval.
units.reusable_pattern: It is easy to find that [attributes] are all in [range]. Therefore, we believe that [item] belongs to [class]
reusable_elements: Its attributes all fall in [range]. We therefore assign [item] to [class]

reusable_elements: Accuracy is [value] on [validation set]

units.source_excerpt: We try to find some other interesting features of this dataset, but we do not know where to start. So we search Wordle on social media to get a specific view of this game.
units.reusable_pattern: We try to find some other interesting features, but we do not know where to start. So we search [source] to get a specific view
reusable_elements: To find further features, we looked at [source]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not narrate not knowing where to start

units.source_excerpt: We suppose that there was an influx of new players who were less familiar with Wordle and less likely to try the hard mode, which caused the percentage of hard mode to plummet.
units.reusable_pattern: We suppose that there was [event] who were [trait], which caused [outcome]
reusable_elements: One reading is that [event] caused [outcome]

units.source_excerpt: As shown in the results, by changing the proportion of the test set, the maximum rate of change is 10%, while the RMSE of the models are all less than 1.0, which proves that our model is not sensitive to the change of this parameter and our model is robust and reliable.

prohibited_generalizations: One parameter sweep does not prove reliability

units.source_excerpt: Prophet model provides excellent predictions for small data sets and adjusts the parameters quite freely, thus facilitating more accurate predictions of the number of reports we will have for future dates.
units.reusable_pattern: [Model] provides excellent predictions for [setting] and adjusts the parameters quite freely, thus facilitating more accurate predictions
reusable_elements: [Model] fits [setting] and exposes [parameters], which makes the forecast adjustable
prohibited_generalizations: 'Excellent' and 'quite freely' are not strengths

units.source_excerpt: Multi-objective regression prediction runs long, and the solution results need simple manual screening.
units.reusable_pattern: [Procedure] runs long, and the solution results need [manual step]
reusable_elements: [Procedure] is slow, and the outputs need manual screening
prohibited_generalizations: A one-line weakness understates model risk

units.source_excerpt: By building several models, we have completed an analysis of MCM's statistics based on players' participation in the Wordle puzzles that your website provides daily. We are honored to present you with the results of what we've analyzed.

units.source_excerpt: So that's the summary of our research. We sincerely hope that it can provide you with useful information and look forward to your reply. Thank you!
units.reusable_pattern: So that's the summary of our research. We sincerely hope that it can provide you with useful information and look forward to your reply
reusable_elements: That is the summary. We hope it is useful
